subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a melody-and-accompaniment texture, the accompaniment:
options: Supports the melody with chords or a bass line
questions.explain: The accompaniment supports the main melody, often with chords or a bass line.

questions.q: What is 'syncopation'?
options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: Which Italian dynamic term means 'very quiet'?
questions.explain: Pianissimo (pp) means very quiet, whereas fortissimo (ff) means very loud.

questions.q: What is the difference between a solo and an ensemble performance?
options: A solo is one performer; an ensemble is a group
A solo is loud; an ensemble is quiet
questions.explain: A solo is performed by one player, while an ensemble involves a group performing together.

questions.q: 'Transposition' means:
options: Changing the dynamics of a piece
Moving music up or down to a different pitch or key
questions.explain: Transposition moves a piece of music to a higher or lower pitch (a different key).

questions.q: In the circle of fifths, how many sharps are in the key signature of D major?
questions.explain: D major has two sharps (F sharp and C sharp) in its key signature.

questions.q: What does the term 'tutti' instruct in an orchestral score?
questions.explain: Tutti means 'all', instructing the whole ensemble to play together.

questions.q: Which clef is also known as the G clef and is used for higher-pitched instruments?
questions.explain: The treble (G) clef curls around the G line and is used for higher pitches.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: On a guitar, a 'capo' is used to:
options: Raise the pitch of all strings to play in a different key
questions.explain: A capo clamps across the fretboard to raise the pitch of every string, changing the key.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.

questions.q: In samba, the large bass drum that provides the heartbeat of the rhythm is the:
questions.explain: The surdo is the large bass drum that drives the underlying pulse of samba.

questions.q: 'Legato' means to play notes:
questions.explain: Legato means smooth and connected, with no gaps between notes.

questions.q: A texture described as 'monophonic' has:
options: A single melodic line with no accompaniment
questions.explain: Monophonic texture is a single unaccompanied melodic line.

questions.q: How many beats does a crotchet last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A crotchet lasts one beat in 4/4 time.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: The tempo marking 'andante' indicates a speed that is:
questions.explain: Andante means at a walking pace, a moderate tempo between slow and fast.

questions.q: How many different pitches does a pentatonic scale contain?
questions.explain: A pentatonic scale is made up of five different pitches per octave.

questions.q: A 'click track' used when recording provides:
options: A guide beat to keep performers in time
questions.explain: A click track is a steady metronome beat in the headphones that keeps performers in time while recording.

questions.q: 'Theme and variations' form is one in which:
options: A theme is stated then repeated with changes each time
A single chord is held throughout
questions.explain: In theme and variations a main theme is stated then repeated in altered forms.

questions.q: Two quavers together are worth the same as one:
questions.explain: Two quavers equal one crotchet beat.
